text:
The evidence can't tell us whether a fire caused the loss. It shows that tree cover was lost, but not why.

What it does show: Hansen/UMD mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 (2.23% of the asset). The JRC 2020 forest map agrees on 98% of that area, and later years were observed, so the loss is corroborated. Most of it (68.1 ha) sits in planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), with 13.2 ha outside mapped forest and none in native forest.

What it doesn't show: Hansen's loss layer captures any stand replacement, including harvest, fire, storm, or clearing. Nothing here identifies the cause. Because the loss is mostly in a plantation, harvest is a plausible alternative, but that is context, not evidence.

To test the fire hypothesis, you would need a fire-specific source, such as burned-area products, active-fire detections, or the owner's records for 2021.
